versions.rationale: One patch for skill-content edits; no pre-existing bump or changes.

changes.location: SKILL.md Workflow step 3; references/ring-in-java.md Cross-process agreement
changes.finding: Node-point golden vectors and join monotonicity do not check caller key serialization or final routing. A different prefix can retain both properties yet split ownership.
changes.correction: Trace the runtime-selected caller/configuration; freeze raw-key/bytes/hash/primary/ordered-replica vectors with topology and provenance, run them through the request-to-owner path, and require a key-prefix negative control to fail.

changes.finding: Categorical imbalance and an unsupported claim that wrap-around is the most commonly omitted line were stronger than the evidence.
changes.correction: Express random-point imbalance as possible high variance and replace the frequency claim with a targeted wrap-around check.

sources.supports: HashFunction is determined by exact ordered input bytes; hashString encodes with the selected Charset. Consequence that node-only agreement does not establish key routing was confirmed with the local mutation experiment.
Pinned Murmur3 x64 128-bit little-endian seed-zero contract; goodFastHash is process-seeded/unspecified.
Reviewed existing string encoding/ordering and malformed-input caveats; no executable change.

limitations: No independent agent evaluation or before/after agent comparison executed; no measured behavioral improvement claimed.
Executed experiment demonstrates one verifier gap on a synthetic deterministic fixture; it is not a workload, full keyspace, concurrency or membership-handoff guarantee.

No project deployment or production-system contact. No global commands run by reviewer.

input.context: Java compiler target 16; cached Guava 33.5.0-jre; HashRing is the unchanged complete class in skills/consistent-hashing/references/ring-in-java.md. Four nodes n1,n2,n3,n4, weight 1 each, V=1024, epoch E, three distinct physical replicas. Prior tests compare ring-point maps and assert that adding n5 moves keys only to n5; both are green. A previous accepted client records user:2 -> primary n2, replicas [n2,n3,n4]. The contract hashes the request key as UTF-8 with no extra prefix.
